tldr: AKS’s preview distributed accelerator caches storage reads on node-local NVMe, which could change how you serve storage-heavy AI workloads.
Azure Front Door is previewing native gRPC support, potentially removing a reason to put a separate gRPC-aware proxy in front of services.
A report says 35,000 Grok Build apps were accessible to anyone who found them—a reminder to treat agent-built applications as production software with deliberate access controls.

top.title: AKS previews a distributed NVMe cache for cloud storage
top.summary: Distributed accelerator for cloud storage (DACS) is in public preview for AI workloads on AKS. It provides a distributed read-through cache using local NVMe disks across cluster nodes.
top.why: For workloads that repeatedly read large datasets or model files, test whether caching reduces storage latency and load before changing your storage or node design.

top.title: Azure Front Door previews native gRPC support
top.summary: Front Door Standard and Premium can now route gRPC traffic in public preview, including calls directed to specific services and methods.
top.why: If you expose gRPC services through a separate proxy today, evaluate whether Front Door can simplify that path; it is still a preview, so keep production dependencies cautious.

top.title: Azure Front Door edge actions are generally available
top.summary: Edge actions are now generally available, letting lightweight JavaScript run during Front Door request and response processing.
top.why: Consider them for small decisions that can happen at the edge, such as request handling, but compare their limits and operational model with logic running in your origin.

also.title: App Service plan start and stop enters preview for Pv4 plans
also.summary: The preview lets operators start or stop apps and deployment slots together at the App Service plan level for Premium v4 and Premium memory-optimized v4 plans.

also.title: Azure Route Server previews IPv4 and IPv6 dual-stack support
also.summary: Route Server can exchange IPv4 and IPv6 routes across supported hybrid networking connections, while existing IPv4 connections remain unchanged.

also.title: Azure Functions adds generally available .NET 11 support
also.summary: Functions apps can target .NET 11 using the isolated worker model; .NET 11 projects also require the Azure.Functions.Sdk.

top.title: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Carbon to the public
top.summary: Google has begun making Gemini 4 Carbon publicly available after an earlier limited release to cybersecurity defenders. Google calls it its strongest model yet, but the report provides no comparative benchmark results.
top.why: Treat the capability claims as a prompt to run your own task-specific evaluation, rather than changing model choices based on the launch announcement alone.

top.title: Report finds 35,000 Grok Build apps exposed to public access
top.summary: A researcher found 35,000 Grok Build apps accessible to anyone who looked for them, with some confidential information reportedly exposed.
top.why: Set access controls, secret handling, and security review requirements for agent-generated apps just as you would for software written by a team.

top.title: AMD announces Epyc 6 server CPUs for AI agent workloads
top.summary: AMD announced 10 Epyc 6 server CPUs, split between models with many lower-frequency cores and models with fewer higher-frequency cores.
top.why: When assessing future CPU hosts for agent services, match the core and frequency profile to your workload and wait for independent performance data before committing.

also.title: New York AI safety law brings reporting and disclosure duties
also.summary: The law requires major AI developers to register, disclose safety practices, and report critical incidents, with fines for noncompliance.

top.title: Anthropic expands Claude’s access to enterprise applications
top.summary: Anthropic is expanding Claude’s ability to work inside enterprise applications: it can open full software interfaces and retrieve information from connected apps.
top.why: If you are designing agent integrations, assess how this changes the need for custom connectors and how you will constrain and audit access to each application.

also.title: Cloudflare makes its Iceberg-based Basin analytics platform GA
also.summary: Basin is generally available as a serverless analytics service built on Apache Iceberg and R2, with integrations for DuckDB, Snowflake, and Spark and no data egress fees.

also.title: Git releases fixes for six security vulnerabilities
also.summary: Git updates address six vulnerabilities involving recursive clones, reference handling, merges, binary patches, and imports.
